layers.note: A small tree of dry, poor ground: gravelly outwash, bluffs and rock outcrops; also bogs, which this model does not separate.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 600 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Holds steep bluffs and rocky slopes.

coldest_c.note: Very cold winters borne: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C), as across the boreal forest.

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 11.5 to 24 °C; gone below 9 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 700.

degree_days_5.note: A short growing season suffices: about 450 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 200.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Lodgepole pine grows from the Yukon to Baja California and the Rockies, as shore pine on the coast and to the tree line inland (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
